answer: For a vote on ivory smuggling through an island inlet, enroll voters at one simultaneous in-person session. Observers keep attendees together until enrollment closes, then issue one signed ballot credential per physically present person. Validators check the issuer signature and allow each credential serial once in that election, across all keys. Extra accounts cannot multiply credentials; another vote requires another person to attend for the whole session. Paid recruits can still pool votes, and corrupt observers can issue fictitious credentials.
